description.value: The study examined brain activation, heart rate variability, and their temporal and predictive relationships during paced breathing, psychosocial stress induction, and recovery from stress.

design.value: Each participant underwent a single MRI-scanning session involving a block-design deep-breathing task combined with the Montreal Imaging Stress Task. Heart rate and respiration were continuously monitored, and fMRI, HRV, questionnaire, generalized additive model, and Granger causality analyses were performed.

description.value: 35 healthy participants were recruited through community advertisements; three participants were excluded due to excessive head movement, leading to a sample size of N = 32.

inclusion_criteria.value: no neurological disorder or head injury

exclusion_criteria.value: excessive head movement during scanning (> 4 mm, ± 3° of rotation)

task_description.value: The task consisted of 4 min of unpaced breathing, 4 min of normal paced breathing at 10 breaths/min, 4 min of deep-paced breathing at 5.5 breaths/min, the Montreal Imaging Stress Task involving difficult arithmetic and negative social evaluation, and a 4-min recovery-from-stress block of deep-breathing at 5.5 breaths/min.

presentation_software.value: Presentation V18 (Neurobehavioral Systems, Berkeley, Calif., USA)

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to follow a paced breathing exercise and to solve simple arithmetic tasks and submit their response via a response button box.

stimuli.value: Visual breathing cues, simple arithmetic problems, and feedback regarding submitted responses and relative performance on a mock performance bar.

task_performance_measures.value: Responses to arithmetic problems were submitted via a response button box; feedback was provided as “correct,” “incorrect” or “too slow.”

instrument.value: Prisma Fit 3-T whole-body MR scanner (Siemens Medical Solutions, Erlangen, Germany) equipped with a standard 32-channel head coil

description.value: 40 oblique interleaved slices were acquired parallel to the AC-PC axis using a T2*-sensitive single-shot EPI sequence. A total of 500 images were collected during one single run.

instrument.value: Prisma Fit 3-T whole-body MR scanner (Siemens Medical Solutions, Erlangen, Germany)

description.value: For anatomical reference, high-resolution T1 MPRAGE anatomical images were acquired.

instrument.value: PPG sensor attached to the proximal phalanx of the left index finger; built-in systems provided by the MRI vendor

description.value: Heart rate was continuously monitored during scanning. Local maxima of the PPG signal were automatically detected, and timestamps of PPG peaks were recorded by the MR Scanner.

reason_no_modality_class_used.value: The acquisition was a physiological PPG recording rather than MRI, EEG, fNIRS, or PET.

instrument.value: Inductive plethysmography via a respiratory cushion integrated into a belt; ECG and respiratory sensor unit (PERU)

description.value: Respiration was continuously measured using inductive plethysmography via a respiratory cushion fitted around the participant’s ribcage. The cushion was connected by a pressure hose to the ECG and respiratory sensor unit, which recorded respiration curves in real time.

reason_no_modality_class_used.value: The acquisition was a physiological respiration recording rather than MRI, EEG, fNIRS, or PET.

description.value: fMRI data were pre-processed using SPM12.

steps.value: Exclusion of first four volumes to account for magnetic field for equilibration
Realignment and unwarping to correct for artifacts due to susceptibility-by-movement interactions
Coregistration of T1 images with the mean T2* images
Normalization to MNI space (functional: 3 mm3, anatomical: 1 mm3)
Smoothing of functional images (8 mm Gaussian kernel)

description.value: PPG peak quality was manually inspected; errors in peaks due to ectopic beats or participant movement were identified using a percentage filter and subsequently interpolated. IBI and RMSSD time-series were resampled at the fMRI TR and mean-centered for the sliding-window analysis.

steps.value: Manually inspect the quality of peak detection by overlapping scanner detected peak timestamps over PPG signal
Identify IBI increases or decreases of more than 30% compared to the previous interval
Interpolate errors in peaks due to ectopic beats or participant movement
Resample IBI and RMSSD time-series at the fMRI TR and mean-center them

model_settings.value: Natural log-corrected IBI and RMSSD values; post hoc comparisons used Tukey’s Honestly Significant Difference test.

estimator.value: Tukey’s Honestly Significant Difference (HSD) test for post hoc comparisons

model_settings.value: Block design; different events modeled using boxcar functions; 480 s high-pass filter; individual contrasts were constructed for Relaxation, Stress Reactivity, Stress Recovery Specific Relaxation, Post Stress Relaxation, stress induction versus unpaced breathing, and stress induction versus normal-paced breathing.

estimator.value: One-sample T-tests at group level; paired T-tests comparing first-level results with and without HRV regressors

model_settings.value: Brain activation time series from seven a priori defined ROIs were used as smooth predictor terms to forecast RMSSD and IBI. Experimental condition, subjects, and time points were included as parametric terms. Thin plate regression splines were used, smoothing parameters were estimated using restricted maximum likelihood, and subject and condition were included as fixed effects in the final models.

model_type.value: Granger causality analysis using vector autoregressive models

model_settings.value: For each HRV–ROI pair, bivariate VAR models were fitted; optimal lag order was determined using the Akaike Information Criterion. Significance was evaluated with 1,000 permutations generated by independently shuffling HRV and ROI time series across time points, with Bonferroni correction.

estimator.value: Akaike Information Criterion for lag selection and permutation-based null distribution

model_settings.value: Exploratory, two-tailed correlations with P < 0.05 between differences in experimental-condition IBI and RMSSD values and PSS, TICS-SCSS, and STAI scores.

description.value: 4 min of normal breathing, where participants were free to breathe at their own pace.
4 min of breathing at a normal rate of 10 breaths/min; this block served as the control condition for deep-paced breathing.
4 min of deep-paced breathing at a breathing frequency of 5.5 breaths/min.

Modified Montreal Imaging Stress Task combining high cognitive demand with negative social evaluation; participants solved arithmetic problems under individually calculated time limits and received manipulated performance feedback.
A 4-min recovery-from-stress block of deep-breathing at 5.5 breaths/min.
